entries.originalText: “My Son, thou hast still many things to learn, which thou hast not well learned yet.”
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, you still have many things to learn, which you have not yet learned well.”

entries.originalText: “To place thy desire altogether in subjection to My good pleasure, and not to be a lover of thyself, but an earnest seeker of My will.
entries.modernizedText: “To place your desire altogether in subjection to My good pleasure, and not to be a lover of yourself, but an earnest seeker of My will.

entries.originalText: Thy desires often excite and urge thee forward; but consider with thyself whether thou art not more moved for thine own objects than for My honour.
entries.modernizedText: Your desires often excite and urge you forward; but consider whether you are not moved more for your own objects than for My honor.

entries.originalText: If it is Myself that thou seekest, thou shalt be well content with whatsoever I shall ordain; but if any pursuit of thine own lieth hidden within thee, behold it is this which hindereth and weigheth thee down.
entries.modernizedText: If it is Myself that you seek, you will be well content with whatever I ordain; but if any pursuit of your own lies hidden within you, behold, it is this which hinders and weighs you down.

entries.originalText: “Beware, therefore, lest thou strive too earnestly after some desire which thou hast conceived, without taking counsel of Me; lest haply it repent thee afterwards, and that displease thee which before pleased, and for which thou didst long as for a great good.
entries.modernizedText: “Beware, therefore, lest you strive too earnestly after some desire which you have conceived, without taking counsel of Me; lest perhaps you regret it afterwards, and what pleased you before displease you, though you longed for it as for a great good.

entries.originalText: For not every affection which seemeth good is to be forthwith followed; neither is every opposite affection to be immediately avoided.
entries.modernizedText: For not every affection that seems good is to be followed at once; neither is every opposite affection to be immediately avoided.

entries.originalText: Sometimes it is expedient to use restraint even in good desires and wishes, lest through importunity thou fall into distraction of mind, lest through want of discipline thou become a stumbling-block to others, or lest by the resistance of others thou be suddenly disturbed and brought to confusion.
entries.modernizedText: Sometimes it is expedient to use restraint even in good desires and wishes, lest through insistence you fall into distraction of mind, lest through lack of discipline you become a stumbling block to others, or lest by the resistance of others you be suddenly disturbed and brought to confusion.

entries.originalText: “Sometimes, indeed, it is needful to use violence, and manfully to strive against the sensual appetite, and not to consider what the flesh may or not will; but rather to strive after this, that it may become subject, however unwillingly, to the spirit.
entries.modernizedText: “Sometimes, indeed, it is needful to use violence, and manfully strive against the sensual appetite, and not to consider what the flesh may or may not will; but rather to strive for this, that it may become subject, however unwillingly, to the spirit.

entries.originalText: And for so long it ought to be chastised and compelled to undergo slavery, even until it be ready for all things, and learn to be contented with little, to be delighted with things simple, and never to murmur at any inconvenience.”
entries.modernizedText: And it ought to be chastised and compelled to undergo slavery for so long, even until it is ready for all things, and learns to be content with little, to delight in simple things, and never to murmur at any inconvenience.”
